We are pleased to announce a fully funded PhD position jointly supervised by Prof. Christian Gogu (ISAE-SUPAERO / University of Toulouse, France) and Dr. Evangelos Niforatos, Assistant Professor (Faculty of IDE / TU Delft, The Netherlands):

“Developing a Human-AI Eco-Innovation Framework for Ambitious and Evidence-Grounded Eco-Design in Aviation”

This doctoral research project will investigate how generative AI and human designers can work together to support more ambitious and environmentally sustainable design in aviation.

The research will explore how Large Language Models (LLMs) and related generative AI techniques can be combined with eco-design, Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), engineering constraints, and structured innovation approaches such as TRIZ. Particular attention will be given to evidence-grounded and traceable AI-generated design alternatives, multimodal interaction, and the role of human–AI collaboration in exploring, critiquing, and refining innovative concepts.

The project lies at the intersection of:

•

Generative AI / LLMs

•

Human–AI interaction and co-design

•

Eco-design and eco-innovation

•

Life Cycle Assessment

•

Engineering design

•

Sustainable aviation

The PhD is offered within the BEST (Between Earth and Sky in Toulouse) doctoral programme, funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) COFUND scheme. The first BEST call will fund 19 PhD projects at the University of Toulouse, with doctoral contracts starting in September 2027.

BEST supports interdisciplinary and international doctoral research addressing major societal transformations. This project is positioned within the Sustainable Transitions pillar and combines expertise from ISAE-SUPAERO / University of Toulouse and TU Delft.

Who can apply?

We welcome candidates with a Master's degree in a relevant field such as:

•

Computer Science / Artificial Intelligence

•

Engineering

•

Aerospace Engineering

•

Industrial or Product Design

•

Sustainable Engineering

•

or a related discipline

Candidates should have strong programming and analytical skills and an interest in generative AI and sustainable engineering/design. Experience with machine learning/LLMs, eco-design or LCA, engineering design, or human–AI interaction is an advantage.

Academic requirements:
By the application deadline, candidates must hold a Master's degree or equivalent diploma and must not hold a doctoral degree.

MSCA mobility rule:
Applicants must not have resided or conducted their primary activity (work, studies, etc.) in France for more than 12 months during the 36 months preceding the call deadline. Periods spent in France as a tourist, refugee, or for national service are not counted as residency.

Application deadline: 23 November 2026 at 12:00 PM CET

Apply via:

On the application portal:

•

Select 2026.

•

Choose “Call for Applications 2026/2027 BEST.”

•

For the BEST Pillar, select “Sustainable Transitions.”
